_graph: Verdicts for every soft rule: what actually enforces each one today. This file is the answer half of the inventory; verification/controls/soft-rules.json is the extraction half, generated by `graphcheck softrules --write`. A verdict of hard means a machine decides it; open means nothing enforces it and nothing records it; procedure means an on-demand instruction whose steps are themselves verified. Correction recorded 2026-11-21: DEFAULT_MAIN_FULL_ACCESS_PROMPT and DEFAULT_MAIN_APPROVAL_PROMPT were first judged stale because they name propose_system_change and apply_system_change. Those two are not registered agent tools, but the system change flow is alive in runtime_system_change.go behind a user-approved gate, so the reason was wrong even though the constants were never composed anywhere - they had zero references, which is why they went.

DEFAULT_MAIN_RSI_IDENTITY.why: 3177 bytes of process instruction: when to record friction, when to run the real-model eval, not to poll after a reload, to report the backlog unprompted. Re-read against the code on 2026-11-21, most of it is still unenforced, but the part that is checkable can be: an RSI receipt already records the commit, the files and the checks, so "report every such action" is a record that exists and could be required. The genuinely soft remainder is when to reach for probe_harness and eval, which is a judgement about whether a measurement would change the decision.
DEFAULT_MAIN_RSI_IDENTITY.splits: activation and no-poll are already facts in the receipt; friction discipline and the backlog report are the parts worth making structural.
DEFAULT_MAIN_RSI_IDENTITY.evidence: DescribeActivation produces the receipt the rule says to report; it does not require reporting anything.
DEFAULT_MAIN_RSI_IDENTITY.enforcedBy: nothing; the receipt exists but reporting it is not required

DEFAULT_COMMON_RULES.why: Nineteen bullets. Four have a mechanism a reader can point at: the comment budget (gate.ScanComments plus graphcheck comments), edit anchoring (the edit tool schema requires edits[].oldText), repository search (rg is on PATH and no indexed extension ships) and the PI_* note (they are set). The other fifteen are methodology with no mechanism at all: write the test before the code, choose the highest test level, prefer an existing implementation, make every change verifiable, take the smallest implementation, delete completely, use tool results as evidence. Splitting means converting the few that can become a gate and admitting the rest are judgement.
DEFAULT_COMMON_RULES.enforcedBy: gate.ScanComments for the comment budget; the edit tool schema for edit anchoring; three more of nineteen
DEFAULT_COMMON_RULES.evidence: ScanComments counts directives and explanatory comments; the edit tool declaration requires edits[].oldText.

DEFAULT_WORKER_RULES.why: Corrected: there is no per-node file list. NodeDefinition carries recipe, task, instructions, harness, workspace, access, acceptance, submission, deliverable, integrate, inputs and outputs - and a workspace is a base plus a path, not a file allowlist. So the two loudest sentences, "stay inside the file list of your node" and "never submit a diff that touches a path outside your node file list", describe a scope that does not exist; what the runtime does enforce is that every path in a workspace_commit resolves inside the admitted node worktree (git_integration_commit.go, path containment and no ".."). Also enforced: one valid submission per execution (kernel Submit rejects a second different one as already_submitted) and named outputs only (unknown_output). Not enforced: which files a lane chose to touch, "implement the smallest complete change", "an edit you have not executed is not evidence".
DEFAULT_WORKER_RULES.enforcedBy: the commit path (paths must resolve inside the admitted node worktree) and one submission per execution; there is no per-node file list
DEFAULT_WORKER_RULES.evidence: No NodeDefinition field lists files; commit containment and one-submission-per-execution are real.

DEFAULT_MAIN_RULES.why: Two bullets, both unenforced, and one of them names a mechanism that does not exist. "One node blocked for three rounds, take over yourself" is read by nothing: nodes.stall_count is written by core_task_nodes.go and reported in views, but no code compares it to a threshold or escalates on it - escalation happens on unanswered questions after 30 minutes (core_problem_escalation.go), which is a different trigger. "Say why you chose the graph shape" is advisory: ProposalShapeNotes computes unexplained, duplicated and unwired nodes and core_task_runtime_supervisor.go attaches them to the propose receipt as shapeNotes, but the draft is still recorded, so the note informs and never blocks.
DEFAULT_MAIN_RULES.splits: the shape reason could become a required, non-empty field on propose_graph; the three-round rule is a judgement about when to stop delegating.
DEFAULT_MAIN_RULES.evidence: Nothing reads a stall threshold; shapeNotes is returned beside a recorded draft, not instead of it.

DEFAULT_REVIEWER_RULES.why: "Every judgment carries files: repository-relative paths" is enforced: core_review_policy.go evaluatePolicy rejects a judgment whose files are empty, absolute, or contain "..". The report shape (verdict, reason, published evidence as exact artifact references) is likewise enforced there. What is not enforced is the behavioural half: "do not inspect the implementation transcript" depends on which tools the reviewer was bound, and "report a duplicate path, an incomplete removal, an unverifiable change as defects" is a judgement about the diff. The rule pointed at rules/common.md, which is this repository prompt rather than a project file, so that sentence is stale wording and should go with the split.
DEFAULT_REVIEWER_RULES.enforcedBy: core_review_policy.go evaluatePolicy, for the report shape and the files field
DEFAULT_REVIEWER_RULES.evidence: evaluatePolicy validates files as nonempty repository-relative paths without ".." and requires verdict, reason and evidence.

DEFAULT_NODE_PROMPT.why: Re-read against the runtime: one valid submit per execution is enforced (a second, different submission is refused as already_submitted; an identical retry replays), outputs must be declared by the node (unknown_output) and satisfy their protocol (output_protocol_mismatch), omitted required outputs are refused (missing_required_output), and artifact reads take an exact version. "Code and review references must identify the exact commit" is enforced for the acceptance path: core_graph_acceptance.go compares the judged commit and marks a review stale when it names another. "Respect the recipe rules and host permissions" is the permission engine, not this prompt.
DEFAULT_NODE_PROMPT.enforcedBy: submit refusal codes (already_submitted, unknown_output, output_protocol_mismatch, missing_required_output) and the acceptance commit comparison
DEFAULT_NODE_PROMPT.evidence: Refusal codes exist for each enforced sentence; the acceptance path rejects a review of another commit.

DEFAULT_MAIN_TOOL_GUIDANCE.why: Three sentences. "Do not poll after activation" is real but unenforced: DescribeActivation returns pending_reload and nothing refuses a second change or a poll while it is pending. "Read a skill before applying it" is unenforced: graphcheck skills checks a skill file format, never whether one was read. "get_task_status for a compact read" is advisory by design - both tools work and the cheaper one is a preference.
DEFAULT_MAIN_TOOL_GUIDANCE.enforcedBy: nothing: the pending reload is reported, never enforced
DEFAULT_MAIN_TOOL_GUIDANCE.evidence: DescribeActivation reports the pending reload; no code path consumes it to block anything.

DEFAULT_REVIEWER_TOOL_GUIDANCE.why: This was wrong in the first census and is corrected here. "Never mutate business files" is NOT enforced by tool absence: a reviewer node is described by the same tool table as a worker, and write_file, run_command and the native bash/edit tools are gated only on features.ReadOnly, which the reviewer path never sets. Measured 2026-11-21 with a throwaway probe against DescribeAgentTools(Role:"reviewer"): the surface was read, write_file, list_dir, artifact_list, artifact_read, artifact_publish, run_command, git. What IS enforced is narrower: workspace_commit carries an explicit Role != "reviewer" term, so a reviewer cannot commit. "Do not use an implementation transcript" is unenforced.
DEFAULT_REVIEWER_TOOL_GUIDANCE.enforcedBy: workspace_commit excludes the reviewer role; write_file and run_command do not
DEFAULT_REVIEWER_TOOL_GUIDANCE.evidence: Probe output: reviewer tool surface includes write_file and run_command; only workspace_commit excludes the role.

verification/skills/verify-graph/SKILL.m.why: An on-demand procedure: launch the daemon view-only, drive the app, capture evidence. Its commands are pinned to the CLI that actually exists - TestSkillCommandsExistInHelp fails when the skill documents a command the CLI does not list - and its journeys are the acceptance tests themselves. That is what a skill is for; converting it into a gate would delete the instruction rather than verify it.
verification/skills/verify-graph/SKILL.m.enforcedBy: skilldoc checks the shape; the journeys check that the steps work.
verification/skills/verify-graph/SKILL.m.evidence: The skill test reads SKILL.md, CONTROLS.md, CONTROL_COVERAGE.md and every feature file and fails on a command absent from help.

verification/CONTROL_COVERAGE.md.why: Explains how to read the coverage numbers; the numbers themselves live in controls/coverage.json and controls/COVERAGE.generated.md, which verify-graph cover rebuilds. It is a reader aid, so it stays prose - but its commands are held to the CLI by the same skill test, which is the part that could rot.
verification/CONTROL_COVERAGE.md.splits: the definition of a witness belongs in the generated coverage report; the rest is procedure.
verification/CONTROL_COVERAGE.md.evidence: CONTROL_COVERAGE.md is one of the files the skill test scans for commands.

verification/skills/verify-graph/CONTROL.why: Schema and worked example for controls/inventory.json. The loader is the contract: ReadInventory refuses an unreadable file and an inventory with no controls, and Normalize drops a control missing name, role or page. Because the loader is looser than the document (it silently drops a half-named control instead of refusing it), the document is still the thing that tells an author what a complete entry is.
verification/skills/verify-graph/CONTROL.enforcedBy: the control inventory loader rejects a malformed entry.
verification/skills/verify-graph/CONTROL.evidence: ReadInventory errors on a missing file or zero controls; Normalize drops incomplete controls.

examples/README.md.why: An index of the native graph examples. It is genuinely thin, but the census proposed merging it into FEATURE_MAP.md and that is wrong: FEATURE_MAP.md is generated from the feature index, the route table and the handler declarations, and it mentions no example graph at all (measured: zero matches for "example" or "graphs/"). Examples are not features a user reaches, so a generated feature map is the wrong home for them and this stays.
examples/README.md.evidence: FEATURE_MAP.md contains no reference to examples/ or its graphs.
